text:
Nick Schmaltz has 20 points in 18 games for Utah, and 13 of them have come on the power play. That split is the whole story. With the man advantage he is one of the more dangerous setup men in the league, which fits what Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking saw last season: 9.4 primary shot assists per 60, 91st percentile among forwards.

At five on five it has been rougher. Utah gets just 44% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, and he is 17 points worse than his teammates by that measure. The odd part is that the bounces have gone against him anyway: his team has scored 6.2 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him out there. He himself is finishing hot, 9 goals on 6.5 expected.

So some of this evens out in both directions. Our range has him finishing around 72 points. What we'd watch is whether the even-strength chances come back, because a 30-year-old living on the power play is one cold month from a quiet stretch.
headline: Schmaltz is producing despite his line, not because
